title: Retro game and application discovery
summary: Screen 732 candidate URLs: add 7 projects and defer three leads.
notes: Personally screened 732 repository URLs against the current catalogue, focusing on Amiga and Atari ST games and applications. Reviewed pinned repository trees, documentation and selected source. Original source releases, reverse-engineered reimplementations and independent remakes are identified separately. No binaries or installers executed. No worker, branch or PR used.

sources.reason: JavaScript reconstruction of Scene Generator V2.11, the Amiga fractal landscape application. The author reports pixel comparisons against the original on six sample scenes and adds PNG/ILBM export; an original water texture must be supplied for exact water.

Native AmigaOS port of the DOS game based on JJFFE, with mechanically translated x86 code, an Amiga platform layer and some hand-ported hot routines. It needs original DOS data and the original assembly reference to rebuild.

Cross-platform patch project with editable graphics and 68000 gameplay fixes for both original game versions, including gunner sight, lead, clipping and helicopter support. It patches supplied disks rather than reconstructing the whole game.

Large 68k listing identified by its author as reverse engineered from the hard-disk version of SWOS 96/97. The file contains named structures and disassembler-style references; an independently working rebuild is not established.

Recovered Glen Cumming development partitions containing Alien Bash II assembly, assets and tools, plus other material. This is historical original source preservation, not a reverse-engineered reconstruction.

Large community archive of Atari ST-family source code grouped by language and author, including games, applications and system tools. It mixes original material and linked submodules; provenance and buildability vary by item.

Linux/SDL source for TecnoballZ, a game first developed on the Amiga and subsequently rewritten for Linux by its developers. This is a source release of a rewrite, not a disassembly of the Amiga executable.

Amiga game-specific static recompilation has a Musashi 68000 interpreter fallback for code not translated or changed at runtime, as shown in runtime/cpu_recomp.cpp. Keep for baked-emulation audit rather than promote under the existing preference to skip game-specific emulation.

Java translation of the original Alien Breed 3D II engine keeps a 64 MB emulated 68k RAM model, guest registers and CPU instruction helpers. Record as pseudo-emulation for audit rather than promote as a conventional high-level reconstruction.

The preview repository now only redirects to a hosted game site; its README says the previews have moved. The underlying Amiga RE toolkit is already tracked, and this repository does not expose an independent current reconstruction.
